topic: PM inaugurates Tk1,542cr flood control, drainage, irrigation project in Feni
headline_marked: Tk 15.42bn [[flood control project inaugurated in Feni]] to shield district
headline: Tk 15.42bn flood control project inaugurated in Feni to shield district
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman unveiled the Rehabilitation of Muhuri-Kahua Flood Control, Drainage and Irrigation Project to protect the region from devastating annual floods.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated the Rehabilitation of Muhuri-Kahua Flood Control, Drainage and Irrigation Project (Phase 1) in Feni on Thursday.
The project, approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) at a cost of Tk 15.42 billion, aims to protect the district from devastating floods.
The work includes the re-excavation of approximately 83.5km of rivers and water bodies, and the rehabilitation of about 68km of embankments.
It also involves riverbank protection and the repair of irrigation infrastructure to reduce flood and erosion damage along the Muhuri, Kahua, and Silonia rivers.
The project addresses the annual breach of the Muhuri embankment caused by hilly runoff and floodwater from upstream India, which often submerges vast areas of farmland and homes.
During the visit, the Prime Minister planted a sapling and launched a canal excavation programme at Kheyaghat near Muhuri Bridge in Parshuram Upazila.
caption:
A Tk 15.42 billion project has been launched to end the long-running misery of annual floods in Feni.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated the Rehabilitation of Muhuri-Kahua Flood Control, Drainage and Irrigation Project (Phase 1) in Feni on Thursday.

The project, approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) at a cost of Tk 15.42 billion, aims to protect the district from devastating floods.

The work includes the re-excavation of approximately 83.5km of rivers and water bodies, and the rehabilitation of about 68km of embankments.

It also involves riverbank protection and the repair of irrigation infrastructure to reduce flood and erosion damage along the Muhuri, Kahua, and Silonia rivers.

The project addresses the annual breach of the Muhuri embankment caused by hilly runoff and floodwater from upstream India, which often submerges vast areas of farmland and homes.

During the visit, the Prime Minister planted a sapling and launched a canal excavation programme at Kheyaghat near Muhuri Bridge in Parshuram Upazila.
